data.hypothesis: A portable 8-byte SWAR bit-plane classifier may reduce per-byte control flow on mixed-width inputs by classifying lead and continuation lanes together, comparing shifted continuation requirements, and checking restricted second-byte ranges. If a sequence crosses a block boundary, defer that block and suffix to the strict scalar validator instead of carrying state. This contrasts with the selected T1 parent's ASCII-block skip and the earlier carry-state variants; it is an unmeasured experiment, not a claimed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: Compare mixed-width performance against the selected parent and baseline; correctness alone does not show this block-skip strategy helps.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected T1 parent 1bef6299446e4809 was correct but measured 57.50 µs, versus the 49.62 µs baseline, so its portable 64-bit ASCII-block skip did not improve the reported mixed-width timing.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this whole-block mask candidate with the unchanged official mixed-width n=65536 protocol.

memory_lessons.applicability: A different role's faster hybrid is useful context but does not establish the performance of whole-stream masks.
memory_lessons.claim: The T2 hybrid 31112ea757f04c4a was correct at 39.98 µs; it is a distinct strategy and is not a measurement of this SIMD-mask candidate.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Keep the strategies distinct when comparing controller measurements.

memory_lessons.applicability: Distinguish correctness logs from final runtime status when recording failed carry-state variants.
memory_lessons.claim: The T1 carry-state variant c557b10fc09a4c93 ended runtime_failed with no timing, although its available correctness log lists 18 passing cases; a separate development attempt 0eeba011b99c4165-h02 failed protected correctness at n=1024.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Treat boundary-state handling as unproven until the new no-carry fallback passes controller checks.

data.notes: The candidate is unmeasured. The selected parent 1bef6299446e4809 was correct at 57.50 µs, slower than the 49.62 µs baseline. The T2 hybrid 31112ea757f04c4a measured 39.98 µs but is a different strategy. Prior T1 experiments include c557b10fc09a4c93 (runtime_failed, no timing) and 0eeba011b99c4165-h02 (protected correctness failure at n=1024). Leave official boundary, truncation, ASCII, and malformed-input checks and timing to the controller.
transformations: Retained the strict scalar UTF-8 validator as the correctness control and bounded suffix validator.
Added portable 8-byte SWAR bit-plane extraction and lead/continuation classification without alignment assumptions or target-specific instructions.
Compared shifted continuation requirements per block and checked E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte restrictions.
Delegated from a block boundary to the scalar validator whenever continuation requirements cross that boundary; kept the run ABI, output, and thread budget unchanged.
